description_good_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence#readme` — the README opens with what the project is (the signed-evidence substrate of the presidio-hardened-* family: canonical JSON and SHA-256 content addressing, detached Ed25519 or HMAC-SHA256 signatures, fail-closed verification against a trust store) and the problem it solves (one evidence contract, extracted from four production implementations before they could drift apart).
interact_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence#readme` — README covers obtaining the software (`pip install presidio-evidence`, PyPI), and links `CONTRIBUTING.md` (issues, bug reports, contributing) and `SECURITY.md` (vulnerability reports); issues at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/issues`.
contribution_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md` — documents the fork → branch → PR flow against `main`.
contribution_requirements_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-acceptable-contributions` — style, tests, security-change rules, dependency bar.
documentation_basics_justification: README (Install, Use, CLI, The contract, Verify a checkout), the architecture decision records in `docs/adr/`, the per-consumer migration plan `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `vectors/README.md` for the golden vectors, and `SEMVER.md` (including how to verify an installation).
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is every name in `presidio_evidence.__all__` (each public function carries a docstring), the `presidio-evidence` CLI (`verify`, `keygen`, exit codes) and the shipped JSON Schemas; enumerated in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SEMVER.md#what-is-the-public-api`, with usage in the README "Use" and "CLI" sections.
sites_https_justification: The project site is the GitHub repository and the package is on PyPI, both HTTPS only. The project runs no other hosted site or service.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/issues` — searchable, URL-addressable, open, no proprietary client.
english_justification: All docs and issue handling in English.
maintained_justification: Releases 0.5.1 and 0.5.0 on 2026-11-02 (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/releases`, PyPI), 0.4.0 on 2026-10-18 (`CHANGELOG.md`); pull requests merged through 2026-11-02; CI and Dependabot active.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands through a pull request from a pushed branch (direct pushes to `main` are blocked by branch protection); interim work is visible between versions.
version_unique_justification: One version in `pyproject.toml` per release; `publish.yml` refuses to build when the tag does not match it; `CHANGELOG.md` records one entry per version.
version_semver_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SEMVER.md` — Semantic Versioning with the documented pre-1.0 profile; wire schemas are versioned separately per schema id.
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z` (`v0.2.0` through `v0.5.1`, `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/tags`); every tag is an annotated, SSH-signed tag that GitHub shows as Verified.
release_notes_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md` — Keep a Changelog format, hand-written per version with "why it matters" lines, not VCS log output. Earlier notes are in the GitHub releases.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability (CVE, GHSA or similar) has been fixed in any release; no security advisory exists for this repository. The four low-severity findings of the pre-publication audit, fixed before the code was public, are still listed under "Security" in the 0.5.0 entry.
report_responses_justification: Met by the documented process. The repository became public on 2026-11-02 and no bug report from outside the project has been received yet; the issues on file (#1, #3) were opened by the maintainer as tracked work, and #3 was fixed and closed by PR #4.
enhancement_responses_justification: Met by the documented process. No enhancement request from outside the project has been received yet; #1 (tighten the `training-run@1` and `gate-certificate@1` schemas) is a maintainer-filed enhancement tracked in the open and linked from the README roadmap.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability` — private GitHub Security Advisory (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/security/advisories/new`) or security@presidio-group.eu; acknowledgement within 72 hours, fix target 30 days.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months: no security advisory, draft or published, exists for this repository, which was private until 2026-11-02.
build_justification: Standard PEP 517 build with the `hatchling` backend: `python -m build` (or `uv build`) rebuilds the sdist and wheel from source. The Rust conformance crate builds with `cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml`.
build_common_tools_justification: pip, `build` and `hatchling` (release builds use a hash-pinned set, `.github/constraints/release-build.txt`); `cargo` for the Rust crate.
test_justification: 20 pytest modules under `tests/` (about 420 tests: canonical JSON, signing, envelopes end to end, schema conformance, consumer vectors, CLI, key handling, audit regressions, vector byte-stability), a Rust conformance suite (`rust/tests/conformance.rs`, 41 tests, plus 6 unit tests) over the same golden vectors, and `scripts/generate_vectors.py --check` for vector stability. Licensed with the project. How to run: `CONTRIBUTING.md#local-verification`.
test_most_justification: CI enforces 100% statement coverage (`[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100` in `pyproject.toml`, applied by `pytest --cov=presidio_evidence` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Branch coverage is not gated; measured locally at 195 of 196 branches on 2026-11-02.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every push to `main` and every PR: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (ruff, vector check, tests with the coverage gate, `pip-audit`, SBOM on Python 3.11; the test suite on 3.12 and 3.13) and `.github/workflows/ci-rust.yml` (fmt, clippy, conformance tests). `conformance` and `conformance-rust` are required checks on `main`.
test_policy_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests` — functional changes ship with tests; fixes ship with regression tests; wire-format changes add vectors and never edit a published one.
tests_are_added_justification: Example: PR #2 (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/pull/2`, merged 2026-10-25) fixed four audit findings (a trust-store `public_key` usable as an HMAC secret, `TypeError` on a non-ASCII signature, a lone surrogate aborting an envelope, forgeable CLI output) and added `tests/test_audit_2026_10_25.py` plus the vectors `vectors/trust-store/rejected-hmac-with-public-key.json` and `public-key-implies-ed25519.json` in the same change.
tests_documented_added_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests` states the policy that changes adding/modifying functionality ship with tests in the same PR.
warnings_justification: `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` in CI (`ci.yml`); `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the Rust crate (`ci-rust.yml`).
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any finding; `main` is clean.
warnings_strict_justification: ruff with `E`, `F`, `I`, `B`, `UP` and `S` (flake8-bandit), only `S101` excused in `tests/` and `fuzz/`; clippy `--all-targets -- -D warnings` on the Rust crate. CI fails on any finding.
know_secure_design_justification: The design is fail closed (bad evidence verifies as `False`, malformed input raises `EvidenceError`, never a pass), least privilege (no keys held, no state, no network, no logging), complete mediation (the whole envelope is parsed before any ref is verified; the CLI calls the same policy), defence in depth (signer binding, subject binding, reuse floor, tier check, key-type separation) and economy of mechanism (vetted primitives only, one canonical encoding). Argued in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#3-secure-design-principles-applied`. The pre-publication audit was run by the maintainer with tool assistance; there has been no independent review.
know_common_errors_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md` maps forgery, cross-signer replay, subject relabelling, downgrade, tier inflation, key confusion and hostile input to controls (section 1), and input validation, output injection, memory safety, crypto misuse, exposed secrets, TOCTOU file handling, unsafe deserialization, exceptions-as-pass and vulnerable dependencies to named countermeasures (section 4).
crypto_published_justification: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) for content addressing, Ed25519 (RFC 8032) and HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104) for detached signatures.
crypto_call_justification: Ed25519 comes from `cryptography` (`Ed25519PrivateKey`/`Ed25519PublicKey`, optional `crypto` extra); SHA-256 and HMAC from the Python standard library (`hashlib.sha256`, `hmac.new`, `hmac.compare_digest`); the Rust crate uses `sha2`. No primitive is re-implemented.
crypto_keylength_justification: The default is Ed25519 with 256-bit keys (about 128-bit security) and SHA-256 digests, above the NIST 2030 minimum of 112 bits. HMAC-SHA256 keys are supplied by the operator and the library does not enforce a minimum length; HMAC exists for back-compatibility and is documented as a shared-secret mode.
crypto_working_justification: No MD4, MD5, single DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG anywhere in the code.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Security functions use SHA-256, Ed25519 and HMAC-SHA256 only; no MD5, SHA-1 or DES.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project implements no key-agreement or network protocol and makes no network calls.
crypto_random_justification: The only security-relevant random value is a new Ed25519 private key in `generate_ed25519_keypair()` / `presidio-evidence keygen` (`src/presidio_evidence/_keys.py`), from `cryptography`'s `Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()`, which draws on the OS CSPRNG. Ed25519 signing is deterministic (RFC 8032) and needs no nonce.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed over HTTPS from PyPI and GitHub. `publish.yml` publishes through PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no stored API token) after a required reviewer approves the `release` environment; PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is fetched over plain HTTP. Release tags are SSH-signed and GitHub-verified; release assets carry build-provenance attestations.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unpatched medium+ vulnerabilities. `pip-audit` runs in CI on every push and PR (`ci.yml`); Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled, with no open alerts. The runtime has no dependencies; `cryptography` is an optional extra.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has arisen in the project or its dependencies; `pip-audit` would fail CI on one.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks 8.30.1 over the full history (all refs, 55 commits) on 2026-11-02: no leaks. The only key material in the tree is the published test fixtures documented in `SECURITY.md#test-keys-in-this-repository` (allowlisted in `.gitleaks.toml`). GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL for Python (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, results in GitHub code scanning, required check `analyze`) and ruff with the `S` (flake8-bandit) rule set in CI; clippy with warnings denied on the Rust crate.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL for Python (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml`) on every push/PR and weekly, and ruff's `S` (flake8-bandit) security rules as a required CI step; OpenSSF Scorecard (`scorecard.yml`) weekly and on every push to `main` for supply-chain posture.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge; CI blocks on ruff and clippy findings, and there are no open code-scanning alerts.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and PR to `main`, plus a weekly scheduled run; ruff runs on every push and PR.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The automated suite exceeds 80% branch coverage (195 of 196 branches, measured 2026-11-02; branch coverage is measured, not gated) and is applied to every release through CI. An Atheris coverage-guided fuzz harness (`fuzz/fuzz_envelope.py`) drives arbitrary bytes through `load_evidence`, `verify_envelope`, `canonical_bytes` and `is_decimal_string`, asserting that only `EvidenceError` or `ValueError` can escape; `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml` seeds it from `vectors/` and runs it on PRs that touch `src/`, `fuzz/` or `vectors/` (60 s) and weekly (300 s). Its first seeded run (PR #9, 2026-11-02) found a defect in the harness itself, fixed in the same PR; the 60 s run after the fix executed 583,156 inputs at 177 coverage edges with no failure in the library.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Python is memory-safe and the Rust crate is safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). The Atheris harness (`fuzz/fuzz_envelope.py`, `fuzz.yml`) runs regardless, seeded from `vectors/`; its 60 s PR run on 2026-11-02 executed 583,156 inputs with no failure in the library.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests are assertion-based (pytest) and run without `-O`; the fuzz harness also runs without `-O`, so its assertions are checked.
dco_justification: Contributions must carry a DCO `Signed-off-by` line (`git commit -s`), documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#licensing-and-developer-certificate-of-origin-dco`; checked in review (there is no automated DCO check). Inbound = outbound `MIT`. The requirement was adopted in November 2026; earlier commits by the maintainer predate it.
governance_justification: Maintainer-led, single-steward model documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md`: ordinary changes decided on the PR, security-relevant changes (the listed security-sensitive modules, schemas and vectors) need a written rationale and may not weaken a default, API changes follow `SEMVER.md`, disagreements escalate to PRESIDIO Group.
roles_responsibilities_justification: Key roles (steward org, maintainer, security contact, release manager, contributor) documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities`.
access_continuity_justification: Continuity rests on the steward organisation: the repository is owned by the `presidio-v` GitHub organisation, not a personal account; PyPI publishing uses Trusted Publishing bound to this repository and the `release` environment, so no personal API token exists; the release signing key is held in the organisation password manager, with its public half in `allowed_signers`; PRESIDIO Group's access policy provides emergency access (Bitwarden Emergency Access) so a designated trustee can take over the owner credentials and signing key and reassign ownership, code-owner review and `release` approval; the release procedure is written down (`SECURITY.md`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml`); and a second person (`ceoofcyber`) holds write access, code-owner review and `release`-environment approval. URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#project-continuity`.
bus_factor_justification: Two people review, merge and approve releases (`vstantch`, `ceoofcyber`, both code owners and `release`-environment reviewers); repository ownership, the signing key and the release flow are organisation-held, documented, and covered by the emergency-access policy. See `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#project-continuity`.
documentation_roadmap_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence#roadmap` — next 12 months to 2027-Q4: now (consumers move from vendored code to the PyPI package, OpenSSF silver), next (producers dual-emit `evidence-ref@2` and `@3`, consumers then demand `@3` per gate; tighter `training-run@1` and `gate-certificate@1` schemas, issue #1), later (a `capability-grant@1` vector once its producer exists; the remaining consumers onto the package).
documentation_architecture_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md` — components (Layer 0, Layer 1, keys, CLI, Rust crate, contract trees), producer and consumer flows, trust boundaries; linked from the README.
documentation_security_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SECURITY.md` (threat model, invariants, reporting, release verification), `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md` (threat table, out-of-scope assumptions, design and weakness arguments), `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`, and the design rationale in `docs/adr/` (ADR-0001 to ADR-0006).
documentation_quick_start_justification: README "Install" (`pip install presidio-evidence`, or `[crypto]` for Ed25519), "Use" (a complete sign-then-verify example) and "CLI" (`verify`, `keygen`); `SEMVER.md#verifying-an-installation` runs the shipped golden vectors against an installed package.
documentation_current_justification: Docs are updated in the same PR as the code they describe (`CHANGELOG.md` per version, `SEMVER.md` public API, ADRs, `PRESIDIO-REQ.md` delivery status), and the README, `SECURITY.md` and `SEMVER.md` describe the current 0.5 line.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence#presidio-evidence`, project 16243) next to the OpenSSF Scorecard badge; the badge image renders the current level, so a newly earned level appears without an edit.
maintenance_or_update_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions` states which lines are supported (0.5.x current; 0.4.x security fixes only while consumers move); `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SEMVER.md` documents the upgrade path, what counts as a breaking change and the per-schema wire stability rules.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability` — reporters are credited in the advisory and the `CHANGELOG.md` entry for the fix unless they ask not to be. No external report has been received yet.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability` — private GitHub Security Advisory or email intake, acknowledgement within 72 hours, fix target 30 days, fixes to the wire contract coordinated with consumers before disclosure.
test_policy_mandated_justification: Formal written policy at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests`: functionality changes ship with tests; bug fixes include a regression test; wire-format changes add vectors. Enforced in review and by the 100% statement-coverage gate.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the full suite on every push and PR (full gate on Python 3.11, tests on 3.12 and 3.13), including `tests/test_envelope_end_to_end.py`, the consumer vectors (one per conforming family repository, `tests/test_consumer_vectors.py`) and the vector byte-stability check; `ci-rust.yml` runs the Rust conformance suite over the same vectors.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Policy requires a regression test with every bug fix. In the last 6 months the product-code defect fixes were the four audit findings fixed in PR #2 (`https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/pull/2`), and all four carry regression tests (`tests/test_audit_2026_10_25.py`) or vectors (`vectors/trust-store/`). The only other fix in that period concerned CI configuration (the SBOM command flag).
test_statement_coverage80_justification: CI gate: 100% statement coverage (`[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100` in `pyproject.toml`, applied by `pytest --cov=presidio_evidence` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
coding_standards_justification: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#style` — ruff (lint and format, configured in `pyproject.toml`: line length 100, target Python 3.11) and `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy` for the Rust crate.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `cargo fmt --check` and clippy run in CI on every PR, inside the required checks `conformance` and `conformance-rust`.
installation_common_justification: `pip install presidio-evidence` (or `pip install 'presidio-evidence[crypto]'` for Ed25519) from PyPI.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#local-verification` — create a venv, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`, then the ruff and pytest commands; `cargo` commands for the Rust lane.
build_repeatable_justification: The wheel is bit-for-bit reproducible: rebuilding `v0.5.0` from the tagged source (`git archive v0.5.0`, `uv build --wheel`) on 2026-11-02 gave a wheel whose SHA-256 (`81203afc…ddc9a`) matches the PyPI file exactly, and two rebuilds matched each other. Release builds use a hash-pinned backend (`.github/constraints/release-build.txt`, `python -m build --no-isolation`) and SHA-pinned Actions; the package is pure Python with no runtime dependencies. The sdist was not compared.
build_standard_variables_justification: A pure-Python package built by `hatchling`; no compiler or linker is invoked. The Rust crate is a non-distributed conformance lane (`publish = false`) with no `build.rs`.
build_preserve_debug_justification: No compiled artefacts are distributed; the wheel is pure Python (`py3-none-any`).
build_non_recursive_justification: A single PEP 517 build; there is no make or subdirectory build.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installed via pip; `DESTDIR`-style conventions do not apply.
external_dependencies_justification: Listed machine-readably in `pyproject.toml` (no runtime dependencies; optional `crypto` = `cryptography>=42`; `dev` and `fuzz` extras) and `rust/Cargo.toml`; release and CI toolchains are hash-pinned in `.github/constraints/*.txt`. A CycloneDX SBOM of the installed wheel with its `crypto` extra is generated, attested and attached to each release by `publish.yml`.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All reused components are PyPI or crates.io packages installed by the package manager (no vendored copies); Dependabot tracks pip, cargo and GitHub Actions updates.
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are kept current by Dependabot (pip, cargo, Actions) with security updates enabled; ruff's `UP` rules flag outdated Python idioms; clippy with `-D warnings` fails on deprecated Rust APIs.
assurance_case_justification: URL: `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md`. Threat model with out-of-scope assumptions and known limitations, five trust boundaries matching `ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`, the secure-design-principles argument and the common-weakness argument. It states that the pre-publication audit was run by the maintainer and is not an independent review.
implement_secure_design_justification: Fail-safe defaults: every verification path returns `False` or raises `EvidenceError`; none returns `True` by default, and `optimistic`/`zk` tiers fail closed. Complete mediation: `verify_envelope` parses the whole envelope before verifying any ref and applies every check to every ref; the CLI uses the same function. Least privilege: no keys held, no state, no network, no logging. Defence in depth: signer binding, `@3` subject binding, the `@1`/`@2` reuse floor, the tier check and key-type separation are independent. Economy of mechanism: Ed25519 from `cryptography`, SHA-256/HMAC from the stdlib, no bespoke crypto. See `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#3-secure-design-principles-applied`.
input_validation_justification: Envelopes are untrusted: `parse_document` (`src/presidio_evidence/_refs.py`) checks a known schema id, each field as a bounded string (≤ 512 chars, no NUL, valid UTF-8), lowercase-hex hashes and signatures, no control characters in `item_id`/`signer`, and the `framework` pattern under `@3`, and raises `EvidenceError` before anything is verified. Trust-store entries are normalised and `public_key` under `hmac-sha256` is rejected; key files are size-bounded. See `ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundaries`.
hardening_justification: `load_private_key` accepts only regular `0600`/`0400` files checked with `fstat` on the opened descriptor, reads at most 256 bytes and never echoes key material; `write_private_key` creates `0600` with `O_EXCL`; HMAC comparison is constant-time; CLI output is JSON-escaped; the Rust crate forbids `unsafe`. Supply chain: SHA-pinned GitHub Actions with least-privilege `permissions:`, hash-pinned release toolchains, Trusted Publishing behind a reviewer-gated environment, secret scanning with push protection.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The signature algorithm is a per-signer trust-store field (`alg`: `ed25519` or `hmac-sha256`, `trust-store@1`), so an operator moves a signer to another algorithm by configuration, and a new algorithm is an additive schema change. The content-hash function (SHA-256) is fixed by the wire format; replacing it would be a new schema major with new vectors (`SEMVER.md#schemawire-stability`), not a runtime switch.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: No key is in the source tree (the published test fixtures in `vectors/` are documented as such). Private keys are supplied at run time from a `0600` file or an environment variable (`load_private_key(path)` / `env=`); trust stores are operator-supplied JSON, and each signer may list several keys, so keys rotate by appending to the list without a new release.
crypto_used_network_justification: The project makes no network calls.
signed_releases_justification: Wheel, sdist and CycloneDX SBOM carry GitHub build-provenance attestations (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo presidio-v/presidio-evidence`), PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations from Trusted Publishing, and release tags are SSH-signed with the public key in `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/allowed_signers`. Documented at `https://github.com/presidio-v/presidio-evidence/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases-and-obtaining-public-signing-keys`. Checked for `v0.5.0` and `v0.5.1` on 2026-11-02 (wheel, sdist and SBOM attestations and the tag signatures all verify).
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag (`v0.2.0` through `v0.5.1`) is SSH-signed with the organisation release key and shown as Verified on GitHub; `git -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=allowed_signers verify-tag <tag>` checks it locally.
sites_password_security_justification: The project runs no site and stores no passwords.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot (pip, cargo, GitHub Actions) with security updates enabled; `pip-audit` on every push and PR (`ci.yml`); OpenSSF Scorecard weekly.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: A library and a command-line tool with no graphical or end-user UI; CLI output is plain text, one line per ref.
internationalization_justification: No user-facing localizable UI; CLI messages are short English diagnostics for developers and operators.
